name: analyze
title: Analyze a render or audio file: loudness, spectrum, pitch, envelope, stereo.
description: Analyze a render or audio file: loudness, spectrum, pitch, envelope, stereo. source: rd_<n> or a file path. Report supple.analysis-report/1.0: loudness (LUFS, LRA, true peak), spectral (centroid, rolloff, flatness, tilt, named band levels relative to the total), harmonic (f0, note, harmonics in dB relative to the fundamental), envelope (attack, decay to -20 dB, release after note-off, onsets), stereo (width, correlation). note_off_s defaults to the end of a render's input. Envelope values (attack, decay, release) describe single notes: render one note to measure them. See describe for errors and examples.

source.description: A render id (rd_1) or an audio file path.

detail.description: summary: key scalars; standard: + percentiles and spectrum; full: + time series.

name: batch
title: Run commands atomically.
description: Run commands atomically. Run commands atomically. See describe for errors and examples.

name: compare
title: Compare two renders or files: notable descriptor changes and timbre distance.
description: Compare two renders or files: notable descriptor changes and timbre distance. Notable changes use fixed thresholds (loudness 1 LU, centroid 10 %, band levels 1.5 dB, harmonics 3 dB, f0 10 cents, ...). ltas_rms_db is the RMS difference of the 1/3-octave spectra after removing the level offset: a pure gain change reads 0. loss is the score the optimizer minimizes and the evaluation scorer judges: the test is loudness-matched to the reference, both are analyzed at their note-off times (note_off_s reports them), and loss.total is the number to get down. A render's note-off is its own input end; give reference_note_off_s / test_note_off_s for files, and one unknown side borrows the other's (note_off_assumed). See describe for errors and examples.

reference.description: A render id (rd_1) or an audio file path.

test.description: A render id (rd_1) or an audio file path.

reference_note_off_s.description: The reference's note-off; defaults to a render's input end.

test_note_off_s.description: The test's note-off; defaults to a render's input end.

loss.description: The score the optimizer minimizes: total, per-term contributions, and the note-off_s used per side.

name: dsp_check
title: Compile a DSP script without saving it; return its diagnostics.
description: Compile a DSP script without saving it; return its diagnostics. Give source (a whole script) or name (one in the library). ok is true when it compiles; plugin then lists its id, name and parameters as the patch shows them. See describe for errors and examples.

kind.description: effect (audio in, audio out) or instrument (notes in)
audio (a sample) or impulse (a Convolver's response)

files.description: the script's files (AudioFile, Convolver), when it has any: give each an absolute path in a patch, {"properties": {"<key>": "/path.wav"}}

name: dsp_export
title: Export a DSP script as a plugin for other DAWs: a CLAP file, or C++ source.
description: Export a DSP script as a plugin for other DAWs: a CLAP file, or C++ source. format clap (the default): copies the platform's script player and embeds the script in its trailer (Linux/Windows) or bundle resource (macOS, re-signed ad hoc with the system codesign tool). The copy is a plugin of its own, under the script's id and name, that plays this version of the script in any CLAP host (it reads no library), written to <folder>/<plugin name>.clap (default: the script's folder, under export/) with the licenses to ship beside it (notices). It runs on this platform, as fast as the player it copies (a debug build's is slow). format source: a C++ project of the plugin template that builds the same plugin (same id, parameters and state) as CLAP and VST3, plus AU on macOS, with the script compiled as C++, written to the empty <folder> (default: the script's folder, under export/<script>-source); its README says how to build it, and license (MIT unless GPL-3.0-or-later) is the license of its own files. Export again after changing the script; an export does not follow the library. See describe for errors and examples.

format.description: clap (default): a plugin file; source: a C++ project

folder.description: an absolute folder to write to (for clap, ~/.clap installs it for this user); for source, empty or new

license.description: source: the license of the project's own files (default MIT)

path.description: the plugin file, or the project's folder

player.description: clap: the script player it was copied from

notices.description: clap: the licenses to ship with the plugin

name: dsp_get
title: Read a DSP script from the library.
description: Read a DSP script from the library.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: dsp_list
title: List the DSP scripts in the library, compiled, with their plugin ids.
description: List the DSP scripts in the library, compiled, with their plugin ids.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: dsp_preview
title: Draw a plugin's editor to a PNG, after a test signal plays through it.
description: Draw a plugin's editor to a PNG, after a test signal plays through it. Give plugin (an id) or script (a name in the library). A fresh instance, set by patch (a merge patch) when given, plays signal -- an effect: sine (the default, at frequency_hz), sweep, impulse, noise or silence, peaking at level_db; an instrument: notes (the default), note or silence -- for seconds while its editor watches, so meters and the script's draw() show what played. Then the editor is drawn without a window, scale times its design size, and saved as a PNG (path; width and height in pixels): read the file to see it. A script with neither editor() nor draw() shows the automatic editor. pointer, if given, acts on the editor first, in its design units (the picture's pixels at scale 1): move (a hover; a drag after a press), press, release, click, double_click, drag (from x, y to to_x, to_y) and wheel (steps notches, up positive), with shift, ctrl or alt held; edits is a merge patch of what they changed, as a user's edits would. problems says what went wrong in the editor's code (a loop stopped by its budget, an index out of range), with the line. Headless pictures use EGL on Linux, Metal on macOS and WGL on Windows; an unavailable renderer returns dsp.no_picture. See describe for errors and examples.

level_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

frequency_hz.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (Hz; accepts quantity strings)

x.description: design units: the picture's pixels at scale 1

y.description: design units: the picture's pixels at scale 1

edits.description: what pointer changed, as a merge patch

name: dsp_test
title: Play test signals or notes through a plugin and measure it: levels, THD, pitch.
description: Play test signals or notes through a plugin and measure it: levels, THD, pitch. Give plugin (an id: a script's, or any effect's or instrument's) or script (a name in the library). A fresh instance, set by patch (a merge patch) when given, plays each signal. An effect: sine (frequency_hz; gain_db and thd_percent), sweep (20 Hz to 20 kHz), impulse (response_db at octave centres), pink noise and silence, each peaking at level_db. An instrument, at velocity 0.8: notes (a note, then a chord), note (A4; pitch_hz, the pitch heard), and silence (no notes); release_ms is how long the sound lasts after the last release. Each reports peak and RMS in dBFS, DC, samples beyond 0 dBFS and denormals; problems says in words what looks wrong (clipping, DC, sound from silence, no output, a note out of tune, sound that never dies away, non-finite samples the framework silenced, a script stopped by its loop budget or indexing outside an array). cpu_percent is measured, so it varies between runs. save: true keeps each output as a WAV (path) for analyze and compare. automation is a list of {param, at_s, value}: semantic patch keys and physical values, as discrete sample-accurate changes applied to every signal (no implicit ramps). automation.max_step is the largest adjacent-sample change in full-scale amplitude; baseline_max_step uses the same render without automation; excess_step is their positive difference. A step above both four times baseline and 0.05 suggests clicks or zipper noise: a screening heuristic, not proof of an artifact or of inaudibility. sidechain supplies a timed key; its middle half is measured against a connected silent key with identical automation: gain_change_db is negative for ducking, null if either output is below -120 dBFS. Slow attack may not settle in that window. Each pass has a fresh instance and initial patch. THD and impulse response are omitted during automation or a non-silent key; gain_db then describes the changing render, not static gain. notes supplies an instrument's sequence ({key, velocity, start_s, length_s}), replacing the notes signal; defaults become notes and silence. Do not combine it with the A4 note signal or select only silence. release_ms starts at its last note-off. Times round to samples at the render rate; spans must fit within seconds. See describe for errors and examples.

signals.description: default: effects five; instruments three, or notes and silence with custom notes

value.description: physical value, enum key or boolean

automation.description: discrete physical-value changes on every signal

level_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

frequency_hz.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server.

notes.description: instrument sequence replacing the notes stimulus

level_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

frequency_hz.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (Hz; accepts quantity strings)

gain_db.description: sine: the fundamental out against in

pitch_hz.description: note: the pitch heard (A4 is 440 Hz)

release_ms.description: an instrument's: sound after the last release

name: dsp_write
title: Save a DSP script to the library and compile it, with diagnostics.
description: Save a DSP script to the library and compile it, with diagnostics. Writes <library>/<name>/<name>.cpp (replacing it), compiles it and returns the compiler's diagnostics, each with a hint. A script that compiles becomes a plugin of the script player under the id its Info gives: plugin.list shows it (listed) and fx.add loads it. Instances already playing it pick up the change within half a second, crossfaded; one that fails to compile leaves them playing the old code. Language: the dsp-language guide. See describe for errors and examples.

name.description: the script's folder and file name

kind.description: effect (audio in, audio out) or instrument (notes in)
audio (a sample) or impulse (a Convolver's response)

files.description: the script's files (AudioFile, Convolver), when it has any: give each an absolute path in a patch, {"properties": {"<key>": "/path.wav"}}

listed.description: plugin.list shows it (the script player is on the plugin path)

name: masking
title: Estimate where one sound masks another (critical bands).
description: Estimate where one sound masks another (critical bands). masker (e.g. the kick) and maskee (e.g. the bass): renders or files at the same sample rate. Per Bark band: % of the maskee's active frames masked and by how much; the three worst bands. An estimate for corrective mixing, not a psychoacoustic model of record. See describe for errors and examples.

masker.description: A render id (rd_1) or an audio file path.

maskee.description: A render id (rd_1) or an audio file path.

name: optimize_start
title: Tune continuous parameters toward a reference sound or a profile (a job).
description: Tune continuous parameters toward a reference sound or a profile (a job). You choose the structure (patch) and which knobs matter; CMA-ES tunes the numbers. params: "auto" (continuous parameters of the modules present, max 32) or keys, optionally {key, min, max} to narrow the search. "auto" searches around each parameter's current value (±2 octaves for frequency, time and pitch-interval quantities, ±25 % of the range otherwise): name keys with min/max when the answer may be far from the current patch. target: {"reference": rd_<n> or file} and/or {"profile": supple.analysis-profile document}; a reference target starts from a smaller initial step than a profile, because the patch is already close. phrase: notation rendered per candidate (default "1: C3:w"; use the reference's phrase when matching a reference). Returns a job: poll job.wait; the result has the best loss per term, the failed-candidate count, changes, a merge patch ({"params": {...}}) for patch.merge, and the best candidate's render. See describe for errors and examples.

params.description: "auto" or a list of keys / {key, min, max}.

name: param_get
title: Read parameter values (physical value and display text).
description: Read parameter values (physical value and display text). keys: semantic keys (e.g. "filter.cutoff"); omit for all. Third-party plugins: CLAP ids or names; values are CLAP values. See describe for errors and examples.

name: param_set
title: Set parameters in physical units; returns the values as applied.
description: Set parameters in physical units; returns the values as applied. values: {key: number | "unit string" | enum key | bool}, e.g. {"filter.cutoff": "1.2 kHz", "filter.mode": "lowpass"}. All values are validated first; nothing changes if any is invalid. Third-party plugins: CLAP id or name keys with CLAP values or {"text": "..."}. Use patch.merge to change several sections at once. See describe for errors and examples.

name: patch_get
title: Get an instance's patch document (changed values or all).
description: Get an instance's patch document (changed values or all). detail changed (default): only values that differ from the defaults, still a complete patch. detail full: every value. Semantic plugins only. See describe for errors and examples.

name: patch_merge
title: Merge a partial patch (RFC 7396) into an instance.
description: Merge a partial patch (RFC 7396) into an instance. patch: only the values to change, e.g. {"params": {"filter.cutoff": "800 Hz"}}; null removes a value (back to its default). Returns the effective change (a minimal merge patch; {} if nothing changed) and a description of the new sound. See describe for errors and examples.

name: patch_set
title: Replace an instance's whole patch; returns a description of the result.
description: Replace an instance's whole patch; returns a description of the result. patch: a complete patch document (see plugin.describe detail full for its schema); missing values take their defaults. Validated fully before anything changes. For partial edits use patch.merge. See describe for errors and examples.

name: plugin_describe
title: Describe an instance: parameters, patch format, and current problems.
description: Describe an instance: parameters, patch format, and current problems. detail summary: parameters grouped as compact 'key = value (range)' lines plus a prose description of the current sound. detail full: every parameter's schema entry with current value and text, and the patch JSON Schema. An entry whose module is not in the patch carries "active": false (add the module with patch.merge to use it). Semantic plugins are programmed with param.set (physical units) or patch.merge. See describe for errors and examples.

status_available.description: The instance supplied its current problems

problems.description: Current plugin problems: code, message, scope, line when known, hint, silent; scope host when unreadable

name: plugin_list
title: List the CLAP plugins the sandbox can load.
description: List the CLAP plugins the sandbox can load. Scans the plugin path once (rescan: true to scan again). filter matches the id or name, case-insensitively. Load one with plugin.load. See describe for errors and examples.

filter.description: Text to match in the id or name.

shadowed.description: Not loadable by id: an earlier location on the plugin path has the same id (load it by path)

name: plugin_load
title: Load a plugin into the chain and return its instance id.
description: Load a plugin into the chain and return its instance id. plugin is an id from plugin.list or a .clap path. An instrument goes first in the chain, anything else last, unless position says otherwise (instruments must stay first). Then describe it with plugin.describe. See describe for errors and examples.

name: plugin_remove
title: Remove a plugin instance from the chain.
description: Remove a plugin instance from the chain. Unloads the instance; its id is not reused. See describe for errors and examples.

name: preset_list
title: List user presets, or a plugin's read-only factory patches.
description: List user presets, or a plugin's read-only factory patches. source: user (default) lists saved presets. source: factory requires plugin and lists its immutable factory patches in declaration order. See describe for errors and examples.

name: preset_load
title: Load a named preset into an instance.
description: Load a named preset into an instance. The preset must belong to the instance's plugin (see preset.list). source: factory applies a read-only factory patch; user (default) loads a saved preset. See describe for errors and examples.

name: preset_save
title: Save an instance's current settings as a named preset.
description: Save an instance's current settings as a named preset. Stores the patch (semantic plugins) or the plugin state. Overwrites a preset of the same name for the same plugin. Names: 1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 space _ . + -. See describe for errors and examples.

name: profile_evaluate
title: Score a render against a target descriptor profile.
description: Score a render against a target descriptor profile. profile: {"schema": "supple.analysis-profile/1.0", "targets": {"<report key>": {"target": x, "tolerance": t, "weight"?: w} | {"min"?: a, "max"?: b}}, "ltas"?: [31 relative dB]}. Keys are dotted report paths such as spectral.centroid_hz.median or harmonic.harmonics_db.3. Returns per-target pass and normalized distance, and a weighted loss (0 = on target). See describe for errors and examples.

source.description: A render id (rd_1) or an audio file path.

name: render
title: Render notes, a MIDI file or an audio file through the chain to a WAV.
description: Render notes, a MIDI file or an audio file through the chain to a WAV. notation: a phrase in the notation (see the notation guide), e.g. "voice lead; 1: C4:q E4:q G4:h | C5:w". midi_file / audio_file: paths (audio at the session rate). bars/seconds override the length; the tail after it is rendered until silence (tail_s caps it). Returns the render id for analyze/compare and the WAV path. See describe for errors and examples.

tempo.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (bpm; accepts quantity strings)

analyze.description: Also analyze the render (see the analyze command); summary is compact (≤ 400 tokens).

name: session_get
title: Show the session: settings, chain, instances and renders.
description: Show the session: settings, chain, instances and renders.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: session_reset
title: Unload every plugin, delete renders and restore default settings.
description: Unload every plugin, delete renders and restore default settings. Not undoable. Saved presets are kept. See describe for errors and examples.

name: session_set
title: Change session settings (rate, block size, tempo, meter, tail limit).
description: Change session settings (rate, block size, tempo, meter, tail limit). Only the given fields change. A rate or block size change reactivates plugins at the next render. See describe for errors and examples.

sample_rate.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (Hz; accepts quantity strings)

tempo.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (bpm; accepts quantity strings)
